 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE RAJIV ROY
ORAL ORDER 3 22-05-2023 Heard the parties.

The petitioners apprehend their arrest in connection with Gaya Kotwali P.S. Case No. 465 of 2017 for the offence registered under sections 420, 406 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code and section 138 of the N.I. Act lodged on 09.10.2017 by the informant, Omkar Nath Mattin.

The prosecution case in brief is that the informant, Omkar Nath Mattin, in the capacity of partner Sushila Devi and Company submitted a written statement on 09-10-2017 at about 4 P. M before the SHO, PS-Kotwali, Gaya stating therein inter alia that petitioner no.1, was conducting his duty as Manager as Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.61127 of 2022(3) dt.22-05-2023 Sasaram office controller.
In May 2016, the informant became ill and in course of treatment till August 2016, he remained in Patna and Delhi.

Further alleged that on 04.09.2016 when the authorities of Tata Chemicals came to make enquiry in godown at sasaram Office, they found that petitioner no.1, has done some wrong, about 800 tonnes urea was misappropriated by the petitioner no.1.

sentences.text: Further alleged that when the authorities of the company put pressure upon the petitioner no.1 and threatened to file criminal case, then petitioner no.2, wife of the petitioner no.1, said that they will dispose of the properties and will deposit the amount of 800 tonnes urea and they had given two cheques bearing no -020198 & 020199 of Bank Of Baroda of dated 20.05.2017 & 22.05.2017 for amount of Rs 55 lacs & Rs. 46,08,600/- respectively.

Further alleged that immediate misappropriated amount was to be transferred to the company, therefore the informant from his own account transferred Rs 10 lacs through draft No- 21980 on 23.01.2017, and on the same very day transferred Rs 10 lacs through draft no- 21981 and Rs 10 lacs through draft no -21982.
Further Rs 5 Lacs on 29.03.2017 through RTGS from Punjab and Sindh bank.
On 04.05.2017 & 05.07.2017 transferred of Rs 10 lacs each through Patna High Court CR.

MISC. No.61127 of 2022(3)
dt.22-05-2023 RTGS and further the informant transferred Rs 13 Lacs through RTGS on 27.05.2017 and on 29.05.2017 informant transferred Rs 20 lacs through RTGS and on 30.05.2017 transferred of Rs 13,08,600/- through RTGS.
Therefore, total of Rs 1,01,08,600/- were transferred in the account of petitioner no.1, then as per instruction of the company the amount had been distributed among the dealers of the company.

Further the persecution alleged that on 03.08.017, the cheques which were given by the petitioners were deposited in the account of informant for clearance but on 05.08.2017, the Bank informed the informant that the cheques were dishonoured on account of insufficient funds.
Thereafter a legal notice was sent to the accused, but till now the petitioner have not given the amount.

Accordingly,
the FIR.
Learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that he was a mere employee and had nothing to do with the said misappropriation of amount for which allegation has been made against him.
A counter affidavit has been filed on behalf of the informant by Mr. Ravindra Kumar Priyadarshi.

In the counter affidavit in paragraph-7, the following facts has been incorporated:-
Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.61127 of 2022(3) dt.22-05-2023 " 7.

That it is stated and submitted that the petitioner no.1 was Manager of the company of the informant and in the absence of the informant, this petitioner no.1 diverted more than 800 tons of fertilizer to different persons for his illegal gain causing huge damage to the informant and his firm.
The petitioner No.1 is only responsible for shortage of fertilizer causing damage.

The cheating and misappropriation will manifest from the fact that the petitioner no.I was Manager in the firm of the informant on the salary of Rs.12,000/-
per month and there was no other source of income except the fact that his wife (petitioner no.1) is a teacher but this petitioner no.1 acquired residential house not only at Varanasi but in Bombay also.
His two daughters completed their studies in a private college entered by way of donation.
The misappropriation of fertilizer was being committed by the petitioner No.1 much before the date on which it is noticed and acquired huge property."

The matter relates to Kotwali (Gaya) P.S. Case No.
465 of 2017 lodged on 09.10.2017.

sentences.text: and on this count alone, this Court deems it fit and proper to dismiss his application for grant of anticipatory bail.
However, learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that he may be permitted to give a chance to file reply to the Patna High Court CR.
MISC. No.61127 of 2022(3) dt.22-05-2023 said counter affidavit which has been served upon him only today.
List this matter one week after vacation.

If no reply is filed on or before the next date of hearing, the petitioner will be liable to pay Rs.
10,000/- to the Patna High Court Legal Services Committee in view of the fact that he has been granted interim protection on 11.04.2023 by the earlier bench.
